SearchHow we decideRulings

Macrons

Consonantal i

Theme

Body, health & movement

disease noun

also illness, sickness, catch a disease, infectious disease, epidemic, attack (of illness)

classical

Ter. Ph. 575: senectūs ipsa est morbus
Cic. Fam. 7.26.1: omnīs morbōs reformīdō
Traupman 63, 64

morbus, morbī m.

noun, second declension

disease, illness

To fall ill: in morbum incidere, morbō corripī (see ill); to catch a disease, morbum contrahere (M-O s.v. catch (a disease), from Pliny). An attack of illness: impetus or accessiō (Traupman 62).

Other words

  • aegrōtātiō, aegrōtātiōnis f. — illness (of the body)

    noun, third declension · also used · classical · Cic. Tusc. 4.29: morbum appellant tōtīus corporis corruptiōnem, aegrōtātiōnem morbum cum imbēcillitāte (Lewis & Short)

    Lewis & Short: properly only of the body, and much used in Cicero’s philosophical works; aegritūdō is classically grief.

  • valētūdō, valētūdinis f. — health, and so ill health

    noun, third declension · also used · classical · Traupman 64: (mala) valētūdō, illness

    Good or bad health (see health).

  • pestilentia, pestilentiae f. — an epidemic, a plague

    noun, first declension · also used · classical · M-O s.v. contagious disease (Plin. NH 23.157)

Examples

  • Senectūs ipsa est morbus.

    Old age is itself a disease.Ter. Ph. 575

  • opprime, dum nova sunt, subitī mala sēmina morbī

    crush the evil seeds of a sudden disease while they are newOv. Rem. 81

  • ego autem quom omnīs morbōs reformīdō …

    but I, since I dread every disease …Cic. Fam. 7.26.1

See also ill, health, fever, doctor, treatment, suffer.
